messages:
incidents-bot: [P1] Elevated 95th pct latency for /v1/chat.stream across us-central1 (detected at 2025-11-05T14:12:25Z). AlertID: alert-4532. Affected customers: multiple, spike in queue length on serving nodes.

Priya (on-call): got the page, looking now. seeing a lot of backpressure on the streaming workers. 95p token latency ~1.8s -> 6s.

Arjun (eng-sre): joining. can you paste the latest tail of the runtime logs? grabbing node health dashboard.

Priya (on-call): pasting short snippet: ```
[14:11:58] worker-7: Accepting conn from 10.0.12.5
[14:12:01] worker-7: kv-cache miss, loading chunk id=0x4f2
[14:12:04] worker-7: queue length=102, inflight=98
[14:12:06] worker-7: stream send timeout to client id=usr-xx after 3000ms
```

Arjun (eng-sre): queue length >100 on several pods, autoscaler isn't catching up because streaming keeps long-lived connections. throughput falls for non-streaming endpoints too. probable root cause: sudden workload shift to many small streaming requests; batching ineffective due to many open streams.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): I agree. streaming uses persist connections + per-token backpressure; when many clients open streams and then idle between tokens it kills concurrency. Quick mitigation: temporarily disable server-side streaming for public API and convert to buffered responses (non-streaming) for all traffic or at least customer tier free/prod?

Priya (on-call): what's the risk to customers? some realtime apps rely on streaming. we'll need a clear rollback path and communication.

Nate (support): If we flip streams off, chat UIs will get responses in one blob instead of incremental tokens. For big customers using websockets, they may notice a lag bump but it's preferable to timeouts. We should send a status update to affected customers.

Arjun (eng-sre): mitigation plan proposal: 1) apply a runtime feature-flag to disable chunked streaming globally for hosted API (api.streaming.enabled=false), 2) add a temporary rate-limit bump for non-streaming token bursts (so clients don't retry aggressively), 3) canary to 10% of traffic for 5 mins, monitor latency, queue length, and 500s. If stable, ramp to 100% in 10 minutes.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): config path: `redwood.runtime.features.streaming` = true/false. I'll prepare the patch. Also recommend enabling `streaming.connection_timeout=500ms` lower while we test so lingering streams drop earlier.

Priya (on-call): sounds good. who will execute?

Kelsey (eng-runtime): I can push the feature flag change to the config service now. Will run canary via router tags.

Arjun (eng-sre): I'll prepare an emergency rate-limit rule: `rl:streaming_fallback` set on API key tier `free` and `standard` to 10 rps per user for 1m window — to prevent stampedes once we disable streaming. Also will add temporary quota increase for premium customers so they don't fail.

Priya (on-call): Priya taking ownership of customer comms with Nate. I'll post an initial status update in #status and DM top support contacts.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): pushing change now. command used: ```sh
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/flags \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"key":"redwood.runtime.features.streaming","value":false,"scope":"hosted","reason":"incident-4532 mitigation"}'
```

Kelsey (eng-runtime): response: `{ "status": "ok", "change_id": "cfg-9987" }`. Starting canary: router tag `streaming-disabled-canary` -> 10% traffic to nodes with new flag.

incidents-bot: Canary started: change cfg-9987, scope=hosted, pct=10, started_at=2025-11-05T14:21:03Z. Watch windows: latency_95, queue_length, 5xx_rate.

Arjun (eng-sre): applying rate-limit rule now. Using ops-console rule editor. Rule ID rl-2025-11-05-1 applied. Backfill for premium customers done.

Priya (on-call): monitoring dashboards... queue length down from 102 -> 36 on canary nodes, 95p latency on canary 1.4s -> 0.9s. Non-canary nodes still high.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): after 5m check: canary stable. bump to 50% for 3m then 100% if no regressions.

Arjun (eng-sre): agree. also enabling fallback logs to capture any client errors: `runtime.logs.streaming_fallback=true` so we can correlate.

Nate (support): posted status update to affected customers: "We're temporarily switching streaming to buffered responses to stabilize latency. No data loss expected. We expect streaming to return in ~30-60 minutes. Contact support for critical workflows."

Priya (on-call): handoff note for next on-call in 20m: incident-4532 - streaming temporarily disabled; current state: flag off, canary -> 50%, rate-limits applied, queue_length decreasing. Next -> monitor 5xx, latency, and customer tickets.

incidents-bot: Note: Pager escalation suspended while mitigation in effect.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): rolled to 100% at 14:35Z. `cfg-9987` is active globally. Streaming endpoints now return blocking responses. Metrics look good: overall 95p latency down to 0.85s, 5xx incidents reduced from 18/min to 2/min.

Arjun (eng-sre): keeping rate-limits in place for another 30m then gradually relax, but only after no retry storms. Any sign of client retries spiking?

Priya (on-call): retry rate stable. no major new alerts. support: only 6 customers reported UI changes, none are currently critical.

Nate (support): logging ticket updates, reached out to premium customers to offer a status call.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): proposing a controlled re-enable plan: 1) set streaming back to true only for premium tier (10% of traffic) for 10m, monitor; 2) if stable, expand to 50% tier traffic, then global. We should also enable `streaming.connection_timeout=1200ms` to reduce idle connections.

Arjun (eng-sre): +1. also create a follow-up to explore adaptive streaming: drop long-idle streams after 200ms of inter-token idle to avoid this next time. Filing tech debt ticket.

Priya (on-call): okay handing off to Arjun for next 30m. I'll update rotation calendar and add checklist. Arjun, please ping if anything spikes.

Arjun (eng-sre): taking over. will keep monitoring for next hour. Incident status: mitigated (streaming disabled). Postmortem to follow with timeline and recommendation to add per-tenant streaming throttles and better autoscaler signals.

incidents-bot: Incident-4532 status changed to MITIGATED by Arjun at 2025-11-05T14:51:45Z. Postmortem assigned to Kelsey and Arjun.

Priya (on-call): thanks team. I'll draft the initial postmortem summary and customer follow-up plan.

Arjun (eng-sre): quick note for postmortem: include exact config diffs (cfg-9987, rl-2025-11-05-1), canary metrics, and trace examples of long-idle streaming sessions. Also include suggested SDK guidance for clients to avoid long inter-token delays.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): will include the rollback timeline and a small runbook step to toggle streaming per-route so we can disable only affected endpoints next time.

Nate (support): thanks everyone. I'll keep customers updated until streaming is re-enabled.

Priya (on-call): ending handoff thread. Arjun, you have the pager.

Arjun (eng-sre): copying final note: incident resolved for now. follow-ups: postmortem, adaptive stream idle timeout, per-tenant throttles, improve autoscaler to consider stream count.
